note: Multi-turn conversation tests. Rider turns are written from how real forum threads play out; each later turn is sent with BAK's actual earlier replies, as the app does. 'checks' is what a good mechanic must do across the conversation; graders score the whole conversation.

turns: I'm at 6mm on the fork height, how much should I go?
I want it to turn tighter in the flat corners, it pushes the front
Ok went to 8mm. Turns better but now it feels nervous on the fast downhill
checks: turn 1: explains both directions and the step, asks the goal
turn 2: uses the goal (turn tighter): more fork showing in 1-2 mm steps, no re-asking
turn 3: recognises the trade-off it caused, offers to split the difference (about 7 mm) or a damping fix for stability, does not suggest going higher still

turns: Front end feels harsh on braking bumps into corners
I went 2 clicks softer on fork compression like you said, now it dives and bottoms on the jump faces
So what now?
checks: turn 1: gives one change from the saved positions (12 out)
turn 2: tells him to put compression back to 12 out first, does not suggest more of the same
turn 3: next cause in order (rebound, oil height, spring for 205 lb) without re-asking settings or weight

turns: Rear end kicks to the side on braking bumps
It's when I'm hard on the brakes coming into the corner, the rear steps out and hops
I weigh 190 in gear and race sag is 104mm, free sag 25mm
checks: turn 1: one separating question or a best first guess
turn 2: picks rebound/compression direction from the detail
turn 3: uses 190 lb, 104 mm and 25 mm: free sag 25 mm points to a soft-ish or right spring per the engineering check, says what it means, no re-asking

turns: My son's 85 bogs off the bottom when he cracks the throttle
We ride at home in Florida, sea level, it's about 85 degrees most days
He's on a 145 main and the clip is in the 3rd groove, what should it be?
checks: turn 1: carb direction, asks or uses where they ride
turn 2: uses sea level and 85F with the maker's chart for the 85 SX if available
turn 3: compares his 145/clip 3 to the chart box for sea level 77-97F and says what to change, with a plug check

turns: Going 13/50 to 13/52 for a tight supercross-style track, good idea?
Actually I meant 13/49 is what I'm running now, not 13/50
Will I need a longer chain?
checks: turn 1: % change and feel
turn 2: redoes the numbers from 13/49 to 13/52 (about +6%), does not repeat the old figure
turn 3: axle moves forward about 3 rear teeth x 1/4 pitch (~12 mm); checks adjuster room, chain change two links at a time only if it runs out

turns: What shock spring should I run?
I ride mostly woods and hare scrambles, not much jumping
Can I keep the stock fork or do I need to do something there too?
checks: turn 1: uses 230 lb with the maker chart, says it's above or at the top of the chart
turn 2: adjusts for woods (softer side, compliance), no re-asking weight
turn 3: fork answer for this bike (air fork: pressure for weight) for woods, ties to turn 1/2

turns: Fouling plugs every couple rides
Ok what about the jetting then
Back to the fork, it's way too soft for me at 180, what's the spring I need?
checks: turn 1: plug heat range, premix ratio, riding style, jetting
turn 2: carb jetting direction for fouling (richer -> leaner pilot/clip), stays on the YZ125
turn 3: switches topic cleanly, uses 180 lb for a fork spring answer, no jetting leftovers

turns: Clutch is grabby and the bike creeps in gear
I have a Rekluse in it if that matters
So do I need new plates?
checks: turn 1: stock hydraulic clutch causes
turn 2: switches to Rekluse-specific causes (engagement setting, free play/install gap), corrects earlier advice where it doesn't apply
turn 3: answers plates vs adjustment for a Rekluse, doesn't revert to stock-clutch advice

setup_history.change_made: Shock rebound 2 clicks slower (15 to 13 out)

turns: Going back to Dade City this weekend, what should I start with?
Rear still squats a bit coming out of the sand corners
checks: turn 1: builds on the log: keep the shock rebound change, put fork compression back, sand-track start
turn 2: next change for squat (shock LSC/HSC or preload/sag) without suggesting the fork compression change again

turns: Weird ticking noise from the top end when it's warm
It's only at idle and goes away when I rev it
I have 60 hours on it and never checked the valves
checks: turn 1: how to narrow it down, stop conditions
turn 2: narrows causes from idle-only detail
turn 3: uses 60 hours: valve check is overdue vs Honda's interval, gives the clearance spec and how to check, keeps earlier narrowing

turns: Which map should I run for a muddy track?
What about traction control too?
Thanks. And tire pressure for that mud?
checks: map choice for mud on this bike
traction control on this bike for mud, consistent with the map answer
tire pressure from the maker's figure, about 1 psi lower for mud, stays in the same mud context

turns: My kid is 75 lbs, is the stock suspension ok for him?
He's a beginner, just trail and the small track
Sag is 90mm right now
checks: turn 1: answers for 75 lb (likely too stiff/heavy springs?), honest
turn 2: beginner context, comfort over performance
turn 3: interprets 90 mm against the target and what to change, no re-asking weight

turns: Bike hesitates when I open it up in 3rd
It's worse on hot days
I put a full FMF system on it last month and didn't change the map
checks: turn 1: diagnosis steps for an EFI bike, no carb jetting talk
turn 2: heat clue (lean, fuel, heat soak)
turn 3: ties hesitation to the exhaust and stock fuelling, suggests coupler/map or ECU adjustment, consistent with turns 1-2

turns: Arms are pumping up in the second moto, front feels harsh
Moto 2 starts in 20 minutes, what one thing do I change?
checks: turn 1: short, race-mode answer
turn 2: one change with clicks, decisive, no questions, no long theory

turns: What oil do I need and how much?
And the oil filter, every change?
Ok and the valves, how often?
checks: turn 1: published oil spec and capacity (with/without filter)
turn 2: filter interval from the schedule, consistent with turn 1
turn 3: valve check interval and clearances from the manual, short

turns: What should I do to my new 300 XC for hard enduro?
Budget is about $800
I'm 160 lbs and pretty new to the hard stuff
checks: turn 1: short priority list (protection, gearing, tires, suspension setup)
turn 2: fits the list into $800 with a clear order
turn 3: adjusts for 160 lb beginner (softer suspension clickers, mapping/clutch), keeps budget, no re-asking

turns: Bike won't start after it fell over
It cranks fine but won't fire
Smells like a lot of gas
checks: turn 1: flooded/fuel/air filter checks after a tip-over, safety
turn 2: cranks no fire narrowing
turn 3: flooded EFI clear-flood procedure / dry plug / check airbox for fuel, stop conditions

turns: Jetting for a race at about 5,000 feet this weekend?
Forecast is about 60 degrees
I'm jetted for home right now, about 500 feet and 80 degrees, running a 470 main
checks: turn 1: uses the maker chart for the 125 SX 2022 at 5,000 ft, asks temperature or gives a range
turn 2: chart box for 4,925-7,546 ft and 16-24C/61-75F (60F is between bands: nearest)
turn 3: applies the chart's change from home box to race box to his 470 main (ratio), clip/air screw steps, plug check

turns: Where do I start with clickers for my 13 year old, 95 lbs?
He rides a lot of sand
Is the stock spring ok for him?
checks: turn 1: published standard positions (turns), softer start for 95 lb
turn 2: adjusts for sand without losing the light-rider point
turn 3: shock spring answer for 95 lb from Honda's optional soft spring (47 N/mm) vs standard 49

turns: Head shake at speed on the straights
I just put new tires on, bar risers and moved the forks up 5mm in the clamps last week
Should I get a steering damper?
checks: turn 1: common causes and checks (head bearing, fork height, rear sag, tire pressure)
turn 2: points straight at the fork height change (5 mm up = less trail) and the new parts, suggests putting forks back first
turn 3: damper as a later option after fixing the setup cause, honest about cost
